brief.headline: Push GLS Films to ₹290.00/KG — Shrinath's proven price — and protect supply by qualifying Huhtamaki or Constantia as a second laminate source given their distress-zone financials.

priceAsk.summary: Match Shrinath Roto Pack's ₹290.00/KG on our top three laminates SKUs, closing the 1.7% gap.
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG across LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 07, LM ELECTRAL UD 4.4g LS 05, and LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08 — saving ₹3.91 L annually.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for identical spec; GLS charges ₹295.00/KG, a 1.7% premium with no differentiation. Market line for BOPET film substrate sits at 171.60 ₹/kg, well below converted laminate prices, confirming room to move.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt — do not extend credit to a loss-making, over-leveraged supplier.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Our ₹18.97 L working capital is already tied up in 30-day terms; any extension risks ₹9.49 L more for a supplier in the grey zone.

brief.financialLeverage: GLS Films is loss-making with a -3.4% net margin versus the 2.5% peer median, and running a 2.15x debt-to-equity ratio with interest coverage of just 0.06x. Their Altman Z-score of 1.68 puts them in the grey distress zone, flagged by severe legal cases, GST and EPF delays, and a Probe42 score of 2/10. Our ₹2.31 Cr spend is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we have zero volume leverage. Lead with supply security and a credible second source rather than a hard price squeeze that could tip them over — but the ₹290.00/KG benchmark is defensible because Shrinath already delivers it profitably.

evidence.point: GLS charges ₹295.00/KG while Shrinath Roto Pack delivers identical laminates at ₹290.00/KG
GLS posted a net loss in FY2024-25, earning -3.4% net margin against a 2.5% peer median
Their balance sheet carries heavy debt with near-zero interest cover
Altman Z-score places them in financial grey zone with multiple red flags
evidence.figure: Altman Z: 1.68, Health score: D (21/100), Probe42 score: 2/10

evidence.point: GLS already stretches supplier payments well past the peer median
We represent a trivial share of their revenue, giving us no volume leverage
evidence.figure: Our spend as share of their revenue: 0.33%

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC at small scale; B (64/100) health score and ₹2611.64 Cr revenue make it a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets.

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter specializing in pharma blister and sachet laminates; strong second-source fit for GEEP despite D (31/100) health score.

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant with both film substrate AND conversion capability; ₹16492.00 Cr revenue and C (54/100) health score offer deep backup capacity for GEEP at scale.

risks: GLS is loss-making with severe legal cases, GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and high leverage — a hard price push could tip supply continuity; keep second source warm.
Their 0.06x interest coverage and 1.68 Altman Z grey-zone score flag imminent distress risk; qualify Huhtamaki or Constantia now, not when GLS stumbles.
Our ₹2.31 Cr spend is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue — we carry zero volume leverage, so frame the ask around competitive parity (Shrinath's ₹290.00/KG) rather than a volume threat.
Extending payment terms beyond 30 days to a 2.15x leveraged, cash-strapped supplier risks ₹9.49 L more working capital and possible default; hold the line on 30 Days After Receipt.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but Shrinath Roto Pack is delivering identical laminate spec at ₹290.00/KG — we need you at that price to keep the volume flowing your way.
